messages:
sanjay_r: Heads-up — seeing ~0.7% of traffic hitting canary-2026 despite the console showing 0.0% for that rollout. Logs show client header X-Client-Env=stable in most hits.

maria_k: :eyes: can you paste the rollout config and the raw route decision for a sample request?

sanjay_r: Pasting sanitized route config we pushed (snip):
```json
{
  "name": "experiment/checkout-canary",
  "splits": [
    { "variant": "stable", "weight": 0.9993 },
    { "variant": "canary-2026", "weight": 0.0007 }
  ],
  "guards": [
    { "type": "header", "header": "X-Client-Env", "value": "canary" },
    { "type": "sticky", "cookie": "rw_sess" }
  ]
}
```

sanjay_r: UI shows 0.0 because the Console rounds weights to 1 decimal. We assumed guard + header rule would be authoritative and set canary weight to 0, but the config drifted to a tiny fractional weight during a programmatic update.

alex_g: ahhh — fractional weight got introduced by the rollout API because the client that writes the plan mixes float precision. Shouldn't the router treat 0.0007 as essentially 0 when a header guard explicitly matches?

maria_k: Router behavior: guards are evaluated first; if header guard matches, it routes to the guarded variant. If no guard matches, it falls back to weighted split. But if the guard is present AND fractional weight exists, we end up in the weighted path for clients that don't present the header because sticky hashing evens out across the population.

taylor_ops: We also saw some requests where X-Client-Env was present but spelled as x-client-env (proxy lowercasing). Our header-matching is case-sensitive in one code path and case-insensitive in another — resulting in ~0.3% of canary hits with header and ~0.4% without. :grimacing:

maria_k: That explains mixed population. Two separate issues: 1) console rounding hides small non-zero weights, 2) inconsistent header normalization between proxy and routing layer.

alex_g: Short term mitigation: update rollout validation to reject weights < 0.001 unless explicitly flagged, and change Console to display at least three decimal places for weights under 1%. Also add a lint warning when guards exist but non-zero fractional weights exist.

sanjay_r: Agreed. For immediate triage I flipped the canary weight to exactly 0 and pushed a quick schema validation patch to the rollout API. Deploy bot: status?

deploy-bot: deploy/api-rollout-validator v1.2.14 promoted to staging (build 8241). No downtime.

alex_g: Longer term: unify header normalization in the edge proxy and routing layer (lowercase everything at ingest) and add an audit check that compares the Console-visible split vs actual config commit (warn on rounding differences).

taylor_ops: I'll open a tiny RFC for header normalization and add an incident runbook entry describing this fractional-weight risk.

maria_k: Filed: ENG-PLAT-4572 (header normalization + console weight precision). Action items: (1) schema reject tiny weights, (2) console precision change, (3) header normalization RFC, (4) backfill audit that finds any live rollouts with weight < 0.01.

sanjay_r: Thanks all — will monitor telemetry for next 24h and roll back if anything unexpected. :thumbsup:
